title: Patient-reported, Health Economic and Psychosocial Outcomes in Friedreich Ataxia (PROFA 2.0)
summary:
In its typical form, Friedreich's Ataxia leads to severe impairment in early adulthood with significant functional impairment and wheelchair dependence. The increasing functional deficits in people with FA are therefore associated with a reduced health-related quality of life and a growing need for care and support. However, there is little evidence on the impact of Friedreich's Ataxia on health-related quality of life, psychosocial health, and the use of health care services and its costs. Furthermore, the effect of omaveloxolone, the only approved medication for FA, has not been investigated in these domains.

The PROFA project aims to investigate the impact of Friedreich's ataxia on patient-related, health economic, and psychosocial outcomes using a patient-centered e-health app for self-reported data collection. Also, PROFA investigates the impact of Omaveloxolone on these outcomes under real-world conditions.

The PROFA project is an observational study based on baseline face-to-face interviews in six study centers (DZNE site Bonn, RWTH University Aachen, University of Innsbruck, LMU Munich, University Hospital Tübingen, Paris Brain Institute) and a subsequent app-based data collection via an e-health app. In the app-based data collection, subjects will complete health and well-being questionnaires, as well as physical and language tests, periodically over 18 months.

interventions.name: Patients will be informed about the study and enrolled at five study centers. The baseline visit will take place immediately afterward. criteria:
Inclusion criteria:
Genetic diagnosis of FA, Ataxia severity SARA score of ≤30 points, Access to a smartphone or similar digital device, Ability to handle a digital device
Exclusion criteria:
Missing FA diagnosis or presence of another ataxia, Ataxia severity SARA score > 30 points, No access to a smartphone or similar digital device, Limitations in handling a digital device, age < 12 years old
